correctness.rationale: The two-coset set S_t=2Z² union ((1+t,1)+2Z²) has Voronoi cell determined by same-coset nearest constraints [-1,1]² and four opposite-coset sites (t±1,±1); each cell has area 2 and a half-turn exchanges cosets. I independently used the six exact rational-polynomial vertices in the source, verified shoelace area 2, all vertex squared distances 1+t⁴/4, and polygonal second moment (4+2t²-t⁴)/6, yielding Q=(4+2t²-t⁴)/12 and R²=1+t⁴/4. Edge sums give exact P(t)=2t²+2(1+t)sqrt(1+(1-t)²)+2(1-t)sqrt(1+(1+t)²). The substitution u=t² makes P/2=Phi(u)=u+q(u)-4u/q(u) with q=sqrt(2(u+2+sqrt(u²+4))). Direct derivative bounds make Phi strictly convex on [0,1], Phi prime(0)<0, Phi prime(1)>0; hence a unique interior minimum t=0.3532048086279578, P=5.64928854396555. R and Q strictly worsen as t increases (0<t<1), and t in (0,1) is non-Bravais. No global honeycomb optimality claimed.
